Memory.value: I find myself pushing the memory away before I can fully recall it
I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

Negative Appraisals.value: I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me
I feel like an object, not like a person

vignette: Kaius had always prided himself on being a composed and empathetic psychologist. But for months now, he'd been avoiding his favorite wine bar with its familiar scent of merlot and dim lighting. The smell of alcohol itself had become a trigger, instantly transporting him back to that night two years ago when he was brutally raped by a stranger in a deserted alley. Kaius couldn't shake the feeling of being an object, not a person, whenever he caught a whiff of booze. This dehumanization seeped into his self-perception, making him question whether he was still capable of doing the things that defined him as a therapist and a man. As he pushed away memories of the traumatic event, Kaius felt emotionally numb, like a part of him had died. He found himself struggling to connect with his clients on a deeper level, fearing that if they knew what had happened to him, they'd see him as weak or tainted. This sense of emotional numbness was suffocating, making it harder for Kaius to access the memories he desperately tried to keep at bay. When fragments did surface, they were disjointed and nonverbal – more a jumble of sensations than a coherent narrative. He couldn't seem to put the frightening event into words, which only added to his feelings of helplessness. Sirens blaring outside his office window would send Kaius's mind racing, instantly conjuring images of police cars and ambulances rushing to scenes of violence. The sound was inescapable, a harsh reminder that danger lurked everywhere. As he tried to calm himself down, Kaius couldn't help but feel like he was no longer the same person – that he'd been irreparably broken by his attacker. This crippling self-doubt fed back into his memories, making it even harder for him to confront the past. The more he pushed the memories away, the more they seemed to haunt him, perpetuating a cycle of avoidance and emotional paralysis. As Kaius navigated his daily routine, he found himself feeling increasingly uncomfortable in social situations – at parties, with friends, or even during therapy sessions. This growing sense of unease was starting to take a toll on his relationships and work performance. His wife had begun to notice the change in him, gently encouraging Kaius to seek help. It wasn't until he realized that he might lose everything he held dear – his career, his marriage, his very sense of self – that Kaius finally mustered the courage to reach out for therapy. He knew it wouldn't be easy, but he was desperate to break free from the suffocating grip of his negative appraisals and memories, to find a way back to the man he once was.
